security_spec.violation_condition: CoVE host kernel verifies a device measurement transcript (via sbi_covg_get_device_measurements) and subsequently allows the TVM to access the device through CoVE-IO mappings without re-verifying, despite the spec now explicitly permitting the TVM to refetch 'the latest device measurement' — implying the measurement can change at runtime (e.g., firmware update, device hotplug/replacement under the same device_if_id)
security_spec.summary: TOCTOU on device attestation transcript: spec allows re-fetch of changing measurements but kernel may cache a stale verified transcript, letting a later-compromised device bypass attestation

findings.finding: The vulnerability pattern sbi_covg_get_device_measurements|sbi_covg_get_device_attestation matches zero code locations in Linux 7.0-rc5. No CoVE (Confidential VM Extension) host kernel support exists in the mainline tree — no sbi_covg_* calls, no CoVE-IO mappings, no TVM device measurement transcript verification logic. The spec-described TOCTOU race (verify-once-then-map without re-verification) cannot occur because the infrastructure it depends on is absent.
findings.snippet: N/A — zero matches across the entire kernel tree for sbi_covg_get_device_measurements, sbi_covg_get_device_attestation, or any CoVE confidential-computing SBI extensions.
